Who we are

Manufacturing

Choosing a contract manufacturing partner in Nigeria

What to actually check before you hand your formulation to a factory — beyond just the price per unit.

If you're building a supplement or tea brand and looking to manufacture in Nigeria, the factory you choose shapes everything downstream — your product's consistency, your regulatory timeline, and ultimately how your customers experience your brand.

A few things worth checking before you commit: Does the facility run a documented quality control process, or is consistency left to chance batch to batch? Have they taken a brand through NAFDAC registration before, and do they understand what auditors look for? Will they run a small pilot batch before committing you to a large production run? And critically — how do they communicate when something doesn't go to plan?

A manufacturing partner that can answer these clearly, and show you their process rather than just describe it, is usually the safer bet — even if they aren't the cheapest quote on the table.

Regulatory

Understanding NAFDAC registration: a starting guide

A plain-language overview of why registration matters and roughly what the process involves.

Any food, drug, herbal supplement or cosmetic product sold in Nigeria is expected to be registered with NAFDAC — the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control. For a health product brand, this isn't just a legal box to tick: it's often the difference between a product retailers and customers trust, and one they won't touch.

At a high level, the process involves preparing product and facility documentation, demonstrating that production follows Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), and going through product listing and inspection before approval is granted. The exact requirements and timeline depend on your product category, so it's worth treating early guidance as a starting point rather than a fixed rulebook.

Because the paperwork and facility standards can be a lot to navigate alone, many brands work with a manufacturing partner who has already been through the process — which is exactly the kind of support we offer alongside production.

Wellness

The role of organic teas in everyday wellness

A look at the botanical traditions behind our tea blends, and why they've endured.

Long before "wellness" became a marketing word, herbal tea was simply part of daily life across West Africa — a cup brewed from hibiscus, ginger, moringa or bitter leaf, reached for out of habit as much as need.

That tradition is the starting point for our own organic tea blends. Rather than treating herbal tea as a trend, we formulate each blend around ingredients with a long, practical history of everyday use — dried, packed and shipped in a way that keeps that character intact from our facility in Jos to your cup.

A tea can't replace medical care, and we're careful not to claim it can. What it can do is anchor a small, repeatable ritual — the kind that's easy to keep up, precisely because it asks so little.
